outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: advance_member now returns decision 'tree-behind' (DECISIONS: redo|block, block needs --reason; STEPS decide-tree-behind; SIGNAL_VERBS judge) for any move not made, so no gate runs at the base the phase left. member_records() is the one record set for the mover and the recut. The existing redo machinery is reused, not duplicated: apply_answer's 'redo' -> recut_tree, rewritten so every refusal comes before drop_tree: tree_work reads the work via carry_commit (scratch index, records excluded, tree and index untouched, full-index binary patch); carry_beside_work refuses when refs/audit/carry/<task> holds a non-record path the work lacks; recut_conflicts tries 'git apply --cached --3way' in a scratch index at the head and refuses by name listing the unmerged paths. After that it writes the patch to state/drive/redo-<id>.patch, drop_tree, add_tree, 'git apply --3way' in the new tree, recut_wrong checks every carried path the head did not move byte for byte against the work commit, carry_work moves the carry ref to the recut tree only after verification, and the patch is removed. A failure after the drop stops naming the kept patch, and advance() runs nothing in that member's tree while the patch exists (redo_left). tests/test_drive_phase.py: ar-block (ar1-ar8, ar3b, ar6b) added and staged; _ab_red_at_base and _file_wave_executor take optional base/work text. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md 'A wave's edges' paragraph rewritten to the new recut. outcome.descriptive: A task tree the mover refuses to bring to the phase head now stops at a redo decision instead of being gated at its old base, and redo recuts it three-way, refusing by name before anything moves.

testsAdded: ar1: a refused overlapping move records no gate row and stops at tree-behind offering redo, tree and work untouched
ar2: redo recuts at the head with the work merged three-way (a plain apply would refuse it), gates green there, spends no attempt, closes on both edits
ar3/ar3b: a conflicting redo is refused by name, with tree, base, work, carry ref, wave bases and gate rows unchanged, and the decision still stands
ar4: dirty record files in the old tree are never carried (only src/f1.txt carried) and the redo applies
ar5: a failure before the old tree comes down leaves the tree, its index, its work and the carry ref as they were
ar6/ar6b: a failure after the drop names the kept patch holding the work, the carry ref is unchanged, and the next run gates nothing over the tree
ar7: a recut tree whose unmoved carried path does not read as the work did stops the redo by name
ar8: a carry ref holding a path the tree's work lacks refuses the redo before anything moves
